thread:
maya: taking evening handoff now — quick capacity + risk notes for the 18:00-02:00 UTC window. TL;DR: watch Pool-A and the scheduled batch from AcmeCorp at ~21:00 UTC, could push burst limits.

maya: current brief snapshot I pulled a few mins ago:
- Pool-A (inference): 68% reserved, 420/512 burst active
- Pool-B (batch/RTX): 35% reserved, 120/512 burst active
- Queue latency: p50 42ms p95 310ms (model x-large)

oncall-bot: deploy-ci reported small deploy to staging finished 15m ago (sha: a3f4b2). No production deploys scheduled.

simon: thanks — do we have an expected ramp number for AcmeCorp job?

maya: yes — ops scheduled a 2.5M token inference run starting 21:05 UTC; estimated sustained concurrency ~40 streams for ~30m, peaks up to 80 for ~2m. Should add ~60-90 rps (tokens/sec dependent).

rachel: FYI AcmeCorp asked for burst guarantee but we only offered best-effort. If Pool-A hits >85% we should start redirecting lower-priority customers to Pool-C.

maya: exact plan: if Pool-A >85% for >2min, escalate to oncall (page), and manual routing: set route override to Pool-C for customers tagged "non-critical-burst". I can make the override but want someone to ack oncall page flow.

ops-runbook-bot: runbook check: when pool utilization >85% -> step 1: check redis cache health; step 2: increase instance drain threshold; step 3: apply routing override. Link: https://runbooks.internal/pool-overflow

simon: I can be on deck from 20:30-22:30 — can handle the override if needed. If I take it, leave the page to me.

maya: perfect. Simon, if you can monitor from 20:45 to 22:15 that's ideal since the ramp is ~21:00. I'll monitor 18:00-21:00 and then 22:15-02:00.

rachel: small ask — please watch the quantization-workers in Pool-B. Last week a mis-configured job caused cache eviction and bumped latency across the board. If you see steady p95 > 600ms, pause batch jobs (label: batch-suspend) and ping infra.

maya: noted. Quick debug command I use if latency spikes:
```
# list pool usage (internal)
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://internal-api/pools/Pool-A/usage
# tail recent allocation logs
journalctl -u pool-agent -n 200 | grep allocation
```

simon: got it. I'll also pre-warm 8 GPUs from Pool-B into Pool-A hot-pool at 20:50 if utilization looks like it's trending up. That should buy ~10-12 minutes of headroom.

maya: thumbs up. If pre-warm happens, please annotate in the channel with the allocation id so I can track billing/metrics.

simon: will do — allocation id format: alloc-<region>-<ts>. I'll paste when done.

oncall-bot: reminder: monthly quota sweep runs at 23:00 UTC. If we move a lot of GPUs between pools it may trigger quota checks for customers; be mindful for enterprise tenants.

rachel: small note — customer-facing SRE was notified of the Acme run earlier; they requested a short message if we expect any latency > 1s. Simon/maya, please craft a quick preemptive FYI if needed.

maya: will draft a 1-line FYI in #customer-ops if we cross 800ms p95 for more than 2min. Template ready.

simon: ack. I'll update here when I start the pre-warm and paste allocation id.

maya: thanks team — leaving handoff pinned. If anything changes I’ll update. :thumbsup:
